A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ForestFormer3D study. All 20 pages of each version, including supplementary text, equations, tables and figures, support comparison. Relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments, component ablations, regional comparisons and sensitivity analyses in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds external-dataset baseline results and a multi-density training experiment.

M1.justification: The backbone, decoder, ISA-guided queries, one-to-many association, losses and score-based merging remain unchanged. The boundary-removal wording clarifies the existing procedure. Multi-density augmentation is evaluated as a separate training variant rather than incorporated into the proposed core method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine FOR-instanceV2 regions, Wytham woods and LAUTx, with the same segmentation tasks. The added augmentation experiment reuses the original and seven downsampled density conditions already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds ForAINetV2_R16 and TreeLearn to both external-dataset comparisons. These methods already appeared in the FOR-instanceV2 comparison, but their participation on Wytham woods and LAUTx is new. The other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Supplementary Section 5 adds retraining on a mixture of the original resolution and seven downsampled versions, whereas v1 only evaluated density sensitivity. Existing splits and metrics remain unchanged. The newly stated 0.6 threshold for component ablations is a disclosure, not evidence of a revised setting.

E4.justification: New Figure 9 tests whether multi-density training mitigates sparse-input degradation, comparing F1 and mIoU with the original model. The existing component, radius/query-count, threshold and density analyses, along with qualitative error examples, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added experiment also presents point estimates without uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: New Table 2 entries report TreeLearn F1 scores of 66.8 on Wytham woods and 92.1 on LAUTx, versus unchanged ForestFormer3D scores of 75.0 and 90.5. ForestFormer3D therefore becomes second on LAUTx. Figure 9 adds sparse-input gains and dense-input losses from augmentation; Tables 1, 3 and 5 retain their scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and loss equations (1–11) are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive derivation is introduced. The added local/global metric discussion does not provide a revised mathematical definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: FOR-instanceV2, a unified end-to-end segmentation framework, leading individual-tree performance on FOR-instanceV2 and generalization to the two external datasets. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 now acknowledges TreeLearn's lead on LAUTx. Supplementary Section 5 concludes that density augmentation helps some sparse inputs but does not solve density robustness and can hurt dense inputs. Section 7 newly attributes F1 discrepancies to SegmentAnyTree's local versus the authors' global aggregation.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promised code/data release with reported public availability and a project link. Section 3.3 specifies removing masks containing even one point within 0.5 m of the cylinder boundary, and Section 4.3 newly discloses the shared 0.6 ablation threshold. The supplement documents the added density-training recipe.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhou et al.'s TreeStructor to the forest-segmentation citations and bibliography. It also credits SegmentAnyTree's augmentation strategy and discusses its metric aggregation. The broader related-work organization and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the external-results discussion and inference explanation, a shortened affiliation, and new acknowledgements. References move from before the supplement to after its substantive text. Most prose and the section hierarchy are retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 expands with four baseline rows and updated ranking emphasis, and Figure 9 adds the augmentation plot. Existing figure images are retained, with former Figures 9–12 renumbered 10–13. Table 3 and surrounding text move, and references now interleave with supplementary figure pages.

improvement.justification: The expanded external comparison corrects the earlier impression of superiority on LAUTx, while Figure 9 provides useful evidence about augmentation's benefits and limitations. Clarified filtering and ablation settings, together with reported code/data access, improve reproducibility. These targeted gains outweigh the less tidy reference placement; the core method and original results remain stable.
